identity.normalization: 'Aqua/Water/Eau' and 'Parfum/Fragrance' are single entries; packet positions = normalized positions (ID-2). 30 entries.

cleansingStrength.rationale: Low: C6, no prominent strong anionic. Earliest prominent cleansing surfactant is the mild anionic Sodium Methyl Cocoyl Taurate @2 (taurate) with prominent co-surfactants Decyl Glucoside @3, Cocamidopropyl Betaine @4 and Coco-Glucoside @12. Disodium Tetrapropenyl Succinate @14 is in no named C3 class (a succinate, not a sulfosuccinate) and is not a strong anionic in any reading, so it cannot move C6.

conditioningLevel.rationale: Moderate: one meaningful system (Amodimethicone @11, prominent) plus light routes (Starch Hydroxypropyltrimonium Chloride @17, weak refatters Glyceryl Oleate @15, Lecithin @16, Hydrogenated Palm Glycerides Citrate @23; humectant Urea @25). C2 not met: no pearlizing wax or fatty-alcohol route. Counter-signal: early silicone + cationic polymer + humectant are three of the four C2 elements, so high is the neighbor.

excluded: Rosmarinus Officinalis Leaf Oil @6, Mentha Piperita Oil @7 (essential oils, 6.4)
unresolved: Sodium Hydrolyzed Potato Starch Dodecenylsuccinate @10: anionic modified starch (no cationic charge); most plausibly an emulsion stabiliser/thickener for the silicone emulsion; if it acted as a film former it would add a third converging family (toward high)

wLine.alphabeticalRun: positions 11-17 (Amodimethicone, Coco-Glucoside, Coconut Acid, Disodium Tetrapropenyl Succinate, Glyceryl Oleate, Lecithin, Starch Hydroxypropyltrimonium Chloride); does not contain the earliest cleansing surfactant (Sodium Methyl Cocoyl Taurate @2), so it is a tail; second entry Coco-Glucoside @12 is the candidate.
wLine.plausibility: Coco-Glucoside @12: (i) cleansing surfactants @2-4 before it; (ii) same-run entries ignored; after the run (18-29) no cleansing surfactant, alkanolamide or pearlizing wax (PEG-150 Distearate is not a (ii) structurant). No earlier a-c candidate (essential oils and menthol are not candidates).

weightPotential.counterevidence: Toward low: both deposition families sit behind essential oils and cooling agents (Menthol @8, Menthyl Lactate @9, typically low-dose), so the amodimethicone and the cationic starch are likely small amounts. Toward high: two families with a weak mild-surfactant reset; unresolved anionic starch @10.
weightPotential.whyThisBand: Amodimethicone (substantive amino-silicone) plus a cationic starch converge in a mild C6 chassis with weak reset; residue is plausible but bounded.
weightPotential.whyNotNeighborBand: Not low: two distinct families (silicone + cationic_polymer) facing a weak reset; positions alone do not show the combined residue stays below noticeable (W2), and a late silicone is not made lighter by position. Not high: no rich architecture (no payload lipid at all), and both families sit after the low-dose cooling agents, so a coating conclusion is not supported.
weightPotential.confidenceLimitingFactor: Silicone/cationic dose unknown; unresolved anionic starch @10.
weightPotential.rationale: Moderate: silicone + cationic starch converge in a weak-reset mild base; late positions argue lighter.
